output.summary: KEP-2494 proposes conventions for storing Kubernetes manifests and metadata for an operator as container images in OCI-compliant registries, and linking metadata-only images to runnable images. The KEP is in provisional status, dated from 2021-02-15.
output.rationale: There is no standard way to transmit Kubernetes manifests and metadata between clusters or to associate them with runnable images, and existing methods (git, operator-registry bundles, helm, appregistry) are non-standard. Packaging the data as container images gives identity, distribution, replication, signing, and ingress for free. The KEP explicitly defers OCI artifacts because registry, tooling, and kubelet support are lacking, with a migration path planned later.

alternatives.why_not: Not all registries support OCI yet, few registries or tools support OCI artifacts, and kubelet cannot pull an OCI artifact into a cluster. The KEP says it would be desirable to move to OCI artifacts when these roadblocks are removed.

alternatives.option: Keep using git repositories, operator-registry directory bundles, helm charts, or appregistry
alternatives.why_not: These are the non-standard methods the motivation identifies as lacking a common way to associate and transmit manifests and metadata.

evidence.quote: There is no standard way to associate and transmit kube and kube-like manifests and metadata between clusters, or to associate a set of manifests with one or more runnable container images.
There is currently no way for kubelet to pull an OCI artifact into a cluster. This limits the ways in which manifest bundles can be used to offcluster.
None of these problems are insurmountable, and it would be desirable to move to OCI artifacts when these roadblocks are removed.
By standardizing on a container format for this data, we get many other features for free, such as: identity, distribution, replication, deduplication, signing, and cluster ingress.
